passages.original: Finis enim et initium epistolæ quae ad Childebertum regem scripta supponitur, spectat ad Gallias et ad Francorum regem, qui, ut liquet ex alia Pelagii epistola, Rufinum, Romam ad Pelagium papam miserat : qui postulavit ut pontifex vel Childeberto significaret se per omnia B. Leonis scriptis assentiri, vel propriis verbis confessionem suæ fidei ad eumdem destinaret. Id constat ex alia Pelagii ad Childebertum regem epistola, in qua pontifex ait: Veniens Rufinus vir magnificus, legatus excellentiæ vestræ, confidenter a nobis, ut decuit, postulavit quatenus vobis aut beatæ recordationis papæ Leonis tomum a nobis per omnia conservari significare debuissemus, aut propriis verbis nostræ confessionem fidei destinare.
passages.english: For the end and the beginning of the letter which is supposed to have been written to King Childebert concern Gaul and the king of the Franks, who, as is clear from another letter of Pelagius, had sent Rufinus to Rome to Pope Pelagius; and he asked that the pontiff either indicate to Childebert that he assented in all things to the writings of Blessed Leo, or send to him a confession of his faith in his own words. This is established from another letter of Pelagius to King Childebert, in which the pontiff says: "Rufinus, a magnificent man, the envoy of your Excellency, on coming [here], confidently asked of us, as was fitting, that we should either indicate to you that the Tome of Pope Leo of blessed memory is preserved by us in all things, or send a confession of our faith in our own words."

passages.original: Si etiam ipsi, licet in suo sensu abundantes, intra materna tamen positi viscera quærerent veritatem, a nobis repellendi non erant, donec apud eos ratione duce rei veritas elaruisset Sed quia se ab universali Ecclesia diviserunt, sicut beatus Augustinus ait, oMinis catholicus securus eam partem dctestatur, cui Ecclesiam universalem apostolicis sedibus roboratam non communicare cognoscit. Nec enim levigat crimea eorum, magis vero auget, quod eos diu restitisse dixistis, ne apostolicis communicantes sedibus in sua communione reciperent.
passages.english: If they too, although abounding in their own sense, nevertheless sought the truth while placed within the maternal womb, they were not to be repelled by us until, with reason as guide, the truth of the matter had shone forth among them. But since they have divided themselves from the universal Church, as Blessed Augustine says, every Catholic securely detests that party which he knows does not communicate with the universal Church strengthened by the apostolic sees. Nor does it lighten their crime, but rather increases it, that, as you have said, they long resisted receiving into their communion those who communicate with the apostolic sees.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'elaruisset' read as 'claruisset', 'oMinis' as 'omnis', 'dctestatur' as 'detestatur', 'crimea' as 'crimen'.
